items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: I remember when I worked at RCA there was a guy named Steve Sholes and he was involved in pop A&R.

ctx.x: Did the advent of rock & roll change the amount of work you would get either as a player or —

Well now it certainly has, I mean that whole thing developed. I remember when I worked at RCA there was a guy named Steve Sholes and he was involved in pop A&R. And there was ads on Billboard and all sort of back and forth. And he signed Elvis Presley for $50,000, a lot of money in those days. Ten million bucks or more or who knows what it would be today. And it was like his ass was on the line, he said he better produce or his job is gone. It was such a — RCA was a conservative company, you know. And of course…
